key_insight: FREDI jointly optimizes fair wireless/compute allocation and dual-threshold early-exit inference so cooperative edge intelligence can securely detect critical events with near-optimal utility.
engineering_relevance: The framework gives a practical way to balance latency, fairness, security, and scalability in UE–edge–cloud systems for real-time AI workloads.
method: Use dual confidence thresholds at the UE to screen events and early-exit easy cases locally.
Offload critical events securely to the edge server for deeper CNN classification.
Solve a proportional-fair joint optimization over UE–ES association, bandwidth, power, and thresholds with exact threshold search and certified resource allocation.
evidence_signal: Experiments with early-exit MobileNetV2 and ShuffleNetV2 show near-perfect UE fairness, aggregate utility close to a sum-utility benchmark, and Stage-A scalability from 6 to 144 UEs with median solve time below 0.1 s.
watch_item: The approach depends on empirical confidence distributions and mixed-integer optimization, so threshold transferability and real-time deployment complexity may vary across datasets, models, and network conditions.
paper_title: Proportional-Fair Resource Allocation and Dual-Threshold Early-Exit Inference for Secure Cooperative Multi-Layer Edge Intelligence
